title: An unified approach for the (inverted) quantum harmonic oscillator and the Berry-Keating hamiltonian
authors: Fabio Bagarello, Emanuele Balistreri, Sergey Kuzhel
abstract: We propose an unified view to three well known quadratic Hamiltonians widely considered in quantum mechanics, i.e. those of the harmonic oscillator, of the inverted harmonic oscillator, and the Berry-Keating Hamiltonian. We describe an unified approach to determine the discrete spectrum of these operators, and to deduce their (generalized) eigenstates. We also look at these Hamiltonians as the generators of $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$, and of a generalized version of it relevant in presence of non Hermitian generators.
summary: This paper presents a unified mathematical approach to analyze the quantum harmonic oscillator, the inverted harmonic oscillator, and the Berry-Keating Hamiltonian. By mapping these systems onto generators of the $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ Lie algebra, the authors provide a single theoretical framework to determine their spectra and eigenstates across different physical regimes. This unification is achieved using advanced techniques involving generalized function spaces.
main_problem: The paper proposes a unified mathematical framework to analyze three fundamental quadratic Hamiltonians in quantum mechanics: the harmonic oscillator, the inverted harmonic oscillator, and the Berry-Keating Hamiltonian.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that these three Hamiltonians can be unified by treating them as generators of $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ Lie algebras, providing a consistent spectral analysis across different physical regimes.
method: The analysis involves linear transformations of the Hamiltonians into a canonical form and employing advanced mathematical tools, including Lie algebra theory ($\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$) and working in generalized function spaces beyond standard $L^2(\mathbb{R})$.
model_or_system: The models are defined by quadratic Hamiltonians in position ($\hat{q}$) and momentum ($\hat{p}$) operators, specifically $H_{	ext{HO}}$, $H_{	ext{IHO}}$, and $H_{	ext{BK}}$. The analysis extends to general linear combinations of these operators.
key_observables: The spectrum (eigenvalues) of the Hamiltonians, which can be real (HO) or purely imaginary (IHO), and the structure of the associated eigenstates.
important_parameters: The coefficients ($\alpha_0, \alpha_1, \alpha_2$) defining the linear combination of the Hamiltonians, and the diagnostic parameter $\xi$ which determines the nature of the spectrum.
main_assumptions: The analysis requires moving beyond the standard $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ space to a Fréchet space $G$ to properly handle the spectrum of the inverted oscillator.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the unified Hamiltonian $H_\alpha$, establishing the spectral classification via the sign of $\xi$, and then rigorously analyzing the spectrum and algebraic structure by relating the Hamiltonians to the $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ algebra using various sets of generators ($K_j$ and $L_j$).
why_interesting: The unification of these three canonical Hamiltonians under the $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ algebra provides deep structural insight into quantum systems, which is relevant for understanding non-Hermitian or time-dependent quantum dynamics.
